git add src/ir_lower/expr/unset.rs src/ir_lower/stmt/mod.rs src/ir_lower/stmt/static_property_helpers.rs tests/codegen/types.rs tests/codegen/types/property_element_unset.rs && git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(unset): `unset($obj->prop[$key])` had no lowering at all and was refused

The unset dispatch recognised a plain LOCAL receiver and nothing else, so an array held in a
PROPERTY fell through to a synthetic `offsetUnset()` — which a class that does not implement
`ArrayAccess` cannot answer — and the backend refused the call outright: `unset target shape
with 1 lowered operands`. A compile error on ordinary php, and on the container code that
made it worth finding.

The write has to LAND, which is the half a first attempt loses: `HashUnset` publishes a
possibly-relocated table back through the receiver's PLACE, and a `PropGet` reached through
an `Acquire` is a place the backend already resolves — so the removal reaches the object's
own array and nothing else. MEASURED against `php -n` 8.5.6 over nine shapes, including a
value copied out one line BEFORE the unset (which must keep the key) and a second instance
(which must not lose its own).

PACKED storage stays refused, deliberately. Converting it at the unset site is what the
local path does, because PHP does not renumber what survives — but a property's type is one
value for the WHOLE program rather than a flow-sensitive one, so recording that promotion
retroactively rejects the `$obj->prop[] = $v` written ABOVE the unset, with
`Array push requires an array property`. Refusing it is what elephc already did; renumbering
it silently would be worse.
